The track slams with a brutal bassline and razor-sharp synths, capturing the raw energy and frustration that fuels the city’s rebellious spirit. There’s a sense of urgency in every beat, like a riot about to erupt, making it impossible to ignore.

This is the second release from Individual Distortion under Geiger Records, and it solidifies their place as a force in the scene. "Skena!" is not just a track—it’s a statement, a call to arms for those who refuse to be silenced. It is ideal for the dark corners of the night when the city’s facade crumbles and the real energy takes over. Fans of dark techno, industrial rhythms, and the raw pulse of underground culture will feel this track deeply.

As the second release from Geiger Records, "Skena!" continues the label’s mission to spotlight bold, experimental sounds that challenge the norm. This track is for the die-hards of the scene, those who find solace in the noise and chaos, who live for the moments when the music becomes a movement.

Description:
I wrote “stay” walking around Manhattan, from the upper east to gramercy park to the les, singing out loud, ruminating on the girl I was seeing at the time and life at that moment. It was one of those early spring days that were standout gorgeous weather and everything just felt right. By the time I recorded the song in South Georgia that May with the windows wide open in my good friend and producer Dan Hartzog’s flat, dubbed “the Pharmacy” where we recorded most of Keep., the song has been ironed out, and even treated with a mini harmonica solo by me at the end. A few people and YouTube comments have told me that they can hear me smiling on this song, and I can’t help but remember this song with a smile. I think I smiled the entire time making it and any time I play it. Just caught a good snapshot of life with this one. Thanks for reading, listening, and enjoying.

The cover art for this project is an actual painting by my mom Rima whose signature is visible in the corner. The project is all about the things you want to keep close, this felt summed by my moms piece and I was excited and honored when she told me I could use it as the art for the project.

Description:
Gorgeous is the first song I ever did with Reo. I've always looked up to him so getting to release this as a part of Glass House was a super special moment for me. Glass House will always feel like a fun art project to me. We got an AirBnb in Malibu (literally a Glass House) where I invited all my friends and we wrote the full project. In a lot of ways - it was the last project I made before going deeper into electronic music and away from the indie sound I had been focused on for a while beforehand.

We dropped this during a very different era onchain. It was during the heyday of Music NFTs and a time that will be looked upon as the birth of this new creative space. I'm excited to give the track new life by bringing it to Base ahead of Onchain Summer and all the amazing energy that's been created since.

Dive back in time to Glass House - danielallan.xyz/glasshouse

I'm hoping this drop can inspire people to consider reminting their classic drops (with their collectors permission of course!) and inviting a new wave of collectors into the mix in a way that wasn't previously possible.

Keep a close eye on Family Affair for more classics and unreleased music and edits!

Description:
This track is a special one. I initially wrote and recorded to this beat produced by Stoic a couple of months ago before passing it over to my good friend Nat Gem, who I met during my time at the University of Arizona. Nat took some time to brainstorm what his feature would look like. I envisioned some background vocals through the chorus/hook and knew he could whip up something dope. Alongside the background vocals, Nat laid down an epic verse starting at 2:45 of the track.

Nat came down to Tucson from Phoenix, which is about two hours apart. We planned a studio session at OCF Studios here in town and had a lively session with producer & engineer wizard Cecilia. I'm really happy with how this track came out; it's like a fusion of Alternative/Hip-Hop and is laid back yet captivating.

This track and its lyrics evoke a blend of introspection, uncertainty, and a willingness to navigate through the complexities of life and relationships.

Being able to work with such a talented musician and artist like Nat Gem is something I will always be grateful for. Thank you to everyone who supports us on our musical journey. You can certainly expect more music from both of us in the near future!

Description:
our parents are mirrors. in the canvas of life, the mother-daughter relationship unfolds in complex ways as u grow up. "do you see you in me?" echoes that reflection, as i’m acknowledging my roots in the so-called “tree”. there’s a constant string that is tied to the generational echoes of a certain dynamic.

this song is a revelation and acknowledgement that after years of accusations and fiery exchanges, there’s a toxic inheritance that reveals itself to me and in me.

just like you explores the complexity of my own self-discovery within the reflections of my parental influence, acknowledging my struggle to break free while embracing the undeniable kinship in our shared flaws.

and i love you, always, but i don’t want to be like you anymore.

Description:
Meet Craig, Reo Cragun’s alter-ego. “what it’s like to lose” is a sneak peak of what’s next for the LNRZ founder. “what it’s like to lose” foreshadows the artist and producer’s next musical chapter. 

Reviving the character from his 2018 EP Craig, Reo Cragun reintroduces a darker mood and more braggadocious attitude to his sonic palette. “I'm not a very bravado person by nature. I have a pretty simple life, to be honest. Craig is kind of the opposite of that. The side of me that’s extravagant, not afraid to express my thoughts, and has strong opinions–that's the character.”

Bridging the gap between Reo and Craig, “what it’s like to lose,” weaves between the more thoughtful, contemplative Reo and a more impulsive, in-your-face Craig.

----

This is the sixteenth track from HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 1—a compilation album curated by NOISE.

Read interviews with each artist at noisedao.mirror.xyz.

Description:
Damn...this song is so fresh that it still hurts when I listen to it. 
-----.......

I don't usually put out songs so soon after recording (4 days ago in Paris) them because it's my personal preference, but I'm making an exception for the OP contest that I'm submitting to. 
-----.......

I was inspired to step out of my comfort zone...and let me tell you..I'm very uncomfortable.
-----.......

Something I know about myself is that I'm very chronological lol. My mind almost NEEDS to work in order. Of course I've been challenging this part of myself for many years haha, it's a daily practice. 
-----.......

Especially when It comes to my music, I am very much like this. I have a few songs I've recorded before this one and I almost feel like I'm doing them wrong by releasing this one first 😂
-----.......

BUT FUCKKK IT! 
-----.......

this is a very telling song of where I have been in my human experience as of late. I have been on a solo journey for over a month now. I traveled all the way up through Italy and am currently submitting this in a cafe in London,England. 

I didn't realize why I needed to have this journey when I started, I just knew I had to do it.

"I thought I was enough for us" is literally me realizing that I am not the only person who's responsible for making life "right". I've always had this feeling of needing to help someone or feeling like someone needed my help. Of course, through my travels, I have unmasked the true foundation of this feeling. In part, it's a trauma response to being rejected by my father and having my innocence taken away from me at a young age.

This trauma caused a co-dependent mentality to grow, feeling like I needed to be needed in order to have importance or value. 

I can't even explain how much this realization has given me clarity on all the questions I've had in regards to the people that have been in my life or the type of relationships I've harbored (or have been unable to harbor). 

I stepped into these travels with a deep desire to finally get a full understanding of why I couldn't be the person I wanted to be in relation to others. Not only have I discovered the root cause, but I now have a direction. 

I am far from "healed" or "complete", but within the laborious work required to get past the dirt, down to the root, I'm coming away with a vigor and strength like I've never had before. 

I am not enough for us, WE are. 


-----

Historically, this symbol has been used in various contexts, from royal banners to national flags, and has evolved over centuries, reflecting the diverse influences and changes in Iranian society. The Lion and Sun emblem remains a profound representation of Iran's enduring legacy, national identity, and the enduring values of courage and wisdom.

Description:
This is a track about what happens when you take a risk on your friendship and it doesn't work out. Despite the outcome of this relationship, this song is really special to me.

2 Years ago I required surgery on my vocal chords which left me unable to sing. During the lockdowns of Covid, it was incredibly difficult to get the treatment that I needed but I didn't want to give up so I kept writing & working on my craft. This was the first song born during this period. As soon as I got the treatment I needed, I made it my goal to record this song.

I'm releasing it 2 years to the day of its first release to commemorate my return to my music which has since opened a lot of doors. I'd like to think it all started with this one...

Description: I wrote this song as a reminder for my grandfather years ago, who recently passed away. He was a music producer and music marketer who worked with Eminem, Maroon 5, Alicia keys, and more. He inspired me to write music and I even got a cassettes tattoo on my arm because of it. He loved cassettes and vinyls and I used to play with them in his office and it interested me a lot. I loved his 60s music and the vibe of it, especially the choirs and the glitchiness of some of his old tapes. It made me make this song and think about all the happy memories of music that he generated. I am going to release this on my birthday… I really hope y’all enjoy, and get to hear the sounds that remind me of one of my biggest inspirations.

Description:
*tend (seeds will grow)* is an original song I created about self-trust – the difficult yet important task of tending to a truth you have just barely glimpsed, but know in your heart of hearts is the path; it reflects on the energy and faith required to stay the course.

The ambient background in the song was generated directly from a real plant (plant seen in background of album cover design) by capturing data from the plant using sensors.

Welcome to my first Sound NFT :) 

==

You may also explore a limited edition version of this piece that includes an audiovisual, animated artwork here: https://app.manifold.xyz/c/tend

Description:
This song is going to be a free mint and a mintpass to my next song drop early next month. Owning this mint-pass will grant you a discount on my upcoming drop.

This is a simple and raw song i recorded in my bedroom with my small and still, minimalist studio setup evident by the sound of crickets in the background. The fan was on because i still don't have air conditioning, and there's a garden nearby hence the background noise. It's a mashup of two of my songs, Memories and Daisies under the moon. 

The photos are taken by my wife of me when we were visiting a hill station close-by called Ooty, in India.
